"the parent Gauss word restricted to the crossings of H, in the parent's cyclic order" -> field `datum`, first conjunct (stmt 653-656): `(carrierGaussList hP (S ∪ K_H) q_H).filter (· ∈ H) = (geometricGaussList hP).filter (· ∈ H)`. `carrierGaussList q` = the visit part of q's traversal word in the inherited cyclic order, cut at vertex 0 (CarrierWord.lean:120-125), and equals `geometricGaussList` filtered by ownership (`carrierGaussList_eq_filter`, CarrierWord.lean:174-176); `geometricGaussList` is P's Gauss word (def:gauss sm-1:249-257) sorted by the traversal key (GeometricVisits.lean:51-54). Filtering to H gives the double-point word of C_H (its double points being exactly H) — disclosed reading (R-c). Equality of the two lists (same cut) implies the printed cyclic-word equality; faithful, mildly stronger in a harmless way. "together with the parent's per-crossing counter-clockwise half-edge order restricted to the surviving half-edges" -> second conjunct (stmt 657-658): `∀ D, D.Γ = pieceShadow → (∀ x, D.IsPositive x) → D = pieceDiagram` (= `eq_pieceDiagram_of_isPositive` stmt 601-604, from GeoPositiveLift.lean:563-565). The rotation-system half of the datum has no explicit Lean counterpart. It holds by construction — the corner polygon's edges are inherited straight subsegments of P's original edges (GeoPositiveLift.lean:122-128), so at every crossing of H the four half-edge directions, hence their ccw order, are the parent's — but this is not stated. Since the definition "is to be read as naming that pair" and the Lean names a plane realisation of the pair whose word half is pinned and whose rotation half is its actual plane geometry, I judge this non-blocking (listed).
